title: Promoted Listings General: expanded ad-fee attribution ("any buyer clicked")
summary: Before Jan 13, 2026, general-campaign ad fees used Direct and Halo item attribution, based on the buyer's own click. From Jan 13, 2026, the ad fee is charged when a buyer purchases the promoted item and any buyer clicked its general ad in the most recent 30 days.
body_markdown: The item must be promoted at both the time of click and the time of sale, and the fee uses the ad rate in effect at the time of sale. Rule change only; no rate change.
affected_sellers: eBay US Promoted Listings General advertisers; also applies to Canada. Already in use on UK, FR, IT, ES, AU and DE sites.

evidence_details.scope: Applies to Promoted Listings General campaigns only. Priority campaigns are charged per click and aren't affected.
conditions: The item must be promoted at the time of click and the time of sale.
The ad fee uses the ad rate in effect at the time of sale.
US and Canada adopt this attribution on Jan 13, 2026; already used on UK, FR, IT, ES, AU and DE sites.
evidence_details.impact: General-campaign ad fees no longer depend on the purchasing buyer’s own click; any buyer’s click on the promoted item in the most recent 30 days can qualify the sale. No rate change or quantified impact is asserted.

references.title: eBay — Promoted Listings attribution
references.quote: eBay will report an Attributed sale from a general campaign when a buyer purchases the same item that was featured in the ad that was clicked on by any buyer in the most recent 30 days.
references.heading: General campaign strategy

references.title: eBay — Promoted Listings attribution
references.quote: The ad fee is charged when a buyer purchases the promoted item from a general ad that any buyer clicked on in the most recent 30 days. The item must be promoted at the time of click and the time of sale. The ad fee is based on the ad rate in effect at the time of the sale.
references.heading: General campaign strategy
